question_text: How do relational database engines automatically resolve detected deadlocks between two competing transactions?

options.text: Pause both transactions indefinitely until locks expire
Abort (rollback) one transaction designated as the victim and allow the other to proceed
Force both transactions to commit simultaneously
Promote both transactions to administrative privileges

answer_explanation: Database engines use wait-for graph cycle detection or lock timeout detection. Upon finding a deadlock cycle, the engine selects a 'victim' transaction, rolls it back, and returns error code 40P01.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: Database engines use wait-for graph cycle detection or lock timeout detection. Upon finding a deadlock cycle, the engine selects a 'victim' transaction, rolls it back, and returns error code 40P01.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
